title: Finite finitely presented direct image preserves finite presentation
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $f_*\mathcal F$ for its Zariski direct image, defined on an open $V\subseteq Y$ by $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$, with $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through $f^\sharp(V):\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$. If $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module, then $f_*\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation].

source.place: Tag 05B4, label lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, forward implication and its affine proof.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal F$. By the definition of a finite morphism, $f$ is affine. The affine permanence lemma gives that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Applying the quasi-coherent direct-image theorem to $f$ and the given quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ proves that $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent. No Noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 05B4, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, first proof sentence; quasi-coherence supplied by Schemes Tag 01LC, lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent, using Morphisms Tag 01S7, lemma-affine-separated.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine open $V\subseteq Y$ and put $U=f^{-1}V$, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $M=\mathcal F(U)$. By the finite-morphism definition, $U$ is affine and $B$ is a finite $A$-module. Since $f(U)\subseteq V$, the affine-open characterization of local finite presentation gives that $A\to B$ is a finitely presented ring map. Restricting the given local finite presentations of $\mathcal F$ to $U$ shows that $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation: each point of $U$ retains its presentation after intersecting its presenting neighbourhood with $U$. The affine finite-presentation criterion, applied to $\mathcal F$ on $U$, now gives that $M$ is finitely presented as a $B$-module.

source.place: Tag 05B4, affine reduction and final invocation of Properties Tag 01PC, lemma-finite-presentation-module; the ring-map hypothesis is Morphisms Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Apply the finite-extension module-presentation theorem to $A\to B$ and $M$. Its two ring hypotheses were proved in Step 2: $B$ is finite as an $A$-module and finitely presented as an $A$-algebra. Its implication from finite presentation over $B$ to finite presentation over $A$ shows that $M$ is finitely presented as an $A$-module. By the direct-image formula in the statement, $\mathcal G(V)=M$, and $a\in A$ acts on $m\in M$ as $f^\sharp(V)(a)m$; this is exactly restriction of the $B$-module structure along $A\to B$. Thus $\mathcal G(V)$ is finitely presented over $A$.

source.place: Tag 05B4, sentence invoking Algebra Tag 0564, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension, in the direction from the source module to its restricted scalars.

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, Step 3 proves that $\mathcal G(V)$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_Y(V)$. Since $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by Step 1, the reverse implication of the affine finite-presentation criterion gives that $\mathcal G|_V$ is of finite presentation. Every point of $Y$ belongs to an affine open $V$. The local presentations on these opens are therefore local presentations on $Y$: for each point choose its presenting neighbourhood inside $V$, with the same restricted structure sheaf and module. By the definition of finite presentation for module sheaves, $\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 05B4, final sentence invoking Properties Tag 01PC; Modules Tag 01BN, definition-finite-presentation, for the Zariski-local conclusion.
